standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the notion of a K-flat complex, the existence of K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and the two-out-of-three lemma for short exact sequences of complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representative K^bullet chosen at the start and the two applications of two-out-of-three showing L^bullet and E^bullet are K-flat.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness criterion on the last term of a bounded above complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma concluding flatness of the cokernel of a map of flat modules from the vanishing of negative tensor cohomology
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies flatness of N = Coker(K^{a-1} -> K^a) and of the image I in K^a.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pullback of a K-flat complex is K-flat
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma showing that the pullback of a K-flat complex of flat modules along a morphism of ringed sites is again K-flat with flat terms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final assertion by pulling the whole construction back along an arbitrary morphism of ringed sites.

core_obligations: Choose a K-flat resolution and truncate (proof lines 12487-12501): take a K-flat complex K^bullet with flat terms representing E, use that the cohomology of K^{n-1} tensor M -> K^n tensor M -> K^{n+1} tensor M computes Tor_n(E, M) and vanishes for n < a, and apply the flatness criterion to conclude that N = Coker(K^{a-1} -> K^a) is flat; then set E^bullet = tau_{>= a}K^bullet.

Show the truncated complex is K-flat (proof lines 12502-12517): the kernel L^bullet of K^bullet -> E^bullet is ... -> K^{a-1} -> I -> 0 with I the image of K^{a-1} -> K^a, which is flat by the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> K^a -> N -> 0; L^bullet is bounded above with flat terms hence K-flat, and two-out-of-three applied to 0 -> L^bullet -> K^bullet -> E^bullet -> 0 makes E^bullet K-flat.

Prove the final assertion (proof lines 12519-12540): for a morphism of ringed sites f, the complex f^*K^bullet is K-flat with flat terms by the pullback lemma and f^*L^bullet is K-flat as a bounded above complex of flat modules; since the short exact sequence of flat modules pulls back to a short exact sequence, the sequence 0 -> f^*L^bullet -> f^*K^bullet -> f^*E^bullet -> 0 is short exact, and a final two-out-of-three shows f^*E^bullet is K-flat.
proof_roadmap: From tor-amplitude below a, truncate a K-flat resolution above degree a and prove the degree-a cokernel is flat by the last-one-flat criterion.
Check the truncated complex and its kernel are K-flat and apply two-out-of-three.
Pull the construction back along an arbitrary morphism of ringed sites, using the pullback lemma and two-out-of-three again, to get the additional uniformity in the representative.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises tor-amplitude bounded below a as representability by a K-flat complex of flat modules vanishing outside [a, infinity), with the extra property that any pullback of the representative stays K-flat with flat terms (statement lines 12471-12484). The proof (proof lines 12486-12540) truncates a K-flat resolution and derives flatness of the degree-a cokernel from the vanishing of the tensor cohomology below a; the K-flatness of the truncation and, for the final assertion, of all its pullbacks follows by the flatness criterion and two-out-of-three. H2: an explicit truncation plus two applications of two-out-of-three.
